statement: A farm has 6 hens and 4 cows. How many legs do the cows have altogether?

choices.misconception: I counted the cows, not the legs of the cows.
I counted all the animals, the hens and the cows together.
I counted the legs of the hens instead of the legs of the cows.
I added up the legs of every animal on the farm, hens as well as cows.

hints: Read the question again. Which animals does it ask about?
The question gives you more than you need. Find exactly what is being asked, decide which numbers matter, and leave the rest out.
Only the cows matter. Each cow has 4 legs, so count 4 legs for each of the 4 cows.

solutions.reliable: The question asks only about the cows, so the hens do not matter. Each of the 4 cows has 4 legs: 4, 8, 12, 16. The cows have 16 legs. The idea to keep: read the question again before answering, and use only the numbers it asks about.

whyOnTest: Contest questions often include extra numbers, and finding exactly what is asked is a skill in itself.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
